name: NoiseUtils
src_typeComment: Thin convenience layer over Unity's built-in Mathf.PerlinNoise — a single octave of Perlin noise looks fairly uniform/smooth; layering several octaves at increasing frequency and decreasing amplitude (aka Fractal Brownian Motion) gives the more natural, detailed look most "noise-driven" effects actually want (camera shake, wind sway, terrain-ish variation).

src_members.sig: public static float Fbm(float x, float y, int octaves = 4, float lacunarity = 2f, float gain = 0.5f)
src_members.name: Fbm

src_members.sig: public static float Fbm1D(float x, int octaves = 4, float lacunarity = 2f, float gain = 0.5f)
src_members.name: Fbm1D
src_members.comment: 1D convenience overload (e.g. Fbm1D(time) for a wandering value) — samples 2D Perlin along a fixed second axis, since Unity has no native 1D Perlin function.
